title: ROBOFISH Construction Protocol
author: Lars E. Borm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcrciv2w
materials: Medium buffer container (40ml) Connect an IDEX P-655 male luer connector to a Sigma Z116955-1EA gauge 12 non-coring needle. Stick this through a Supelco Supleco 27022 septum cap on a Supelco SU860001 glass vial. Run an appropriate length of tubing from the valve to the luer adapter and connect with an XP-202 fitting and ferrule. When using the system place a small needle through the septum so that the vial does not pull a vacuum when liquid is removed. Connect as many as needed to the valve. For the EEL protocol you need one for the stripping buffer.

Flow cell There are two options for flow cells in the ROBOFISH system. Either the Rebus Biosystems flow cell or the Bioptechs FCS2. The Rebus flow cell comes with its own temperature controller. For the FCS2, temperature is controlled by a recirculating chiller and you can either use the Solid State Oasis (now called UC 160-190) unit or the ThermoCube. Place the flow cell on the microscope stage. Place the temperature controller somewhere that you can connect the cables to the flow cell. The cables can be mounted to the breadboard using a Thorlabs CMS010 base with a Thorlabs CMS011 tie wrap and a M6 bolt. Move the stage around and make sure there is enough free cable to allow full movement. Rebus flow cell Rebus flow cell temperature controller.
Software installation and Operation For the software installation and operation of the system please see the code and instructions on the Github page: https://github.com/linnarsson-lab/ROBOFISH

FCS2 Temperature control Connect at least the bottom heating tubes of the FCS2 to the recirculating chiller. We do not use the top temperature flow option (black ring) because it can pop out when the pressure increases inside the loop. This can happen when you increase the temperature. We have ran successful smFISH experiments using only the bottom tube for temperature control. To connect to the barbed tubing we used Cole-Parmer Silikon Patin (Tygon 3350, ID 3.2, WS 1.6, AD 6.4mm) tubing. The Oasis and ThermoCube units come with a variety of connection options. Please make sure you can couple the soft tubing attached to the FCS2 to the Oasis or ThermoCube unit. Our ThermoCube has a Swagelok connector that required solid tubing so we had a barbed connector for the soft tubing and connected this to solid tubing using a Quick Release fitting from Parker. Temperature sensing of the FCS2 is done using an integrated thermistor which can be read out using a Yoctopuce Yocto-MaxiThermistor unit. On the first port of the Yocto-MaxiThermistor unit connect a supplied thermistor to measure the room temperature. Connect the second port to the middle two slots of the FCS2 using electrical wire and two pins. Fully connected FSC2 on the microscope stage Yoctopuce Yocto-MaxiThermistor

steps.title: Prepare Building Platforms
steps.instruction: Construct two building platforms near the microscope stage. Use a regular wall-mounted shelf and a Thorlabs MB3045/M Aluminum Breadboard (300 X 450mm, M6 screw taps) mounted with two Thorlabs PSY321 Post-Mounted breadboard brackets on a Thorlabs SDH7590 with B7590L microscope table.

steps.title: Install Cold Incubator
steps.instruction: Place a Techne BlocIce cold incubator on the bottom surface, adjusting the breadboard height to be 50mm higher than the incubator. Seal seams and screws with silicon glue to protect electronics from condensation.

steps.title: Mount Syringe Pump
steps.instruction: Mount a Tecan Cavro XCalibur syringe pump onto the breadboard using M6 bolts and a 3D printed base.

steps.title: Construct 2.5ml Reservoir
steps.instruction: Create a reservoir using IDEX XP-3030 tubing (1/8" OD, 1/16" ID).

substeps.instruction: Calculate required length using: length = 2.5 / (π * inner diameter^2). For the specified tubing, the length is 126.3cm.
Cut the tube to length using an IDEX A-327 plastic tubing cutter tool.
Connect the reservoir to the right port of the syringe pump using an IDEX XP-303 1/8" Delrin nut and ferrule.
Mount the reservoir to the breadboard with an M6 bolt using an empty tubing case.

steps.title: Install and Configure Valves
steps.instruction: Position two IDEX MXX778-605 selector valves on the breadboard.

substeps.instruction: Left Valve: Open the ring and install 1/8" connectors in positions Center, 7, 8, 9, and 10. Install 1/16" connectors in remaining positions (remove green o-rings from 1/16" connectors before inserting 1/8" connectors).
Right Valve: Install 1/8" connectors in all ports and close the ring loosely.

steps.title: Connect Reservoir and Valves
steps.instruction: Establish the fluidic path between the reservoir and valves.

substeps.instruction: Insert the reservoir tube into the center of the left valve, pressing it all the way down.
Connect the left valve (suggested port 9) to the center of the right valve using a 15cm piece of 1/8" tubing.

steps.title: Install Degasser and Shut-off System
steps.instruction: Set up the degassing and manual purge line on the breadboard to the left of the valves.

substeps.instruction: Connect a 20cm piece of IDEX 1514L 1/16" OD PFA tubing from a multi-valve port to a Biotech AB Degassi Classic degasser using an IDEX XP202 flangeless fitting and ferrule.
Connect the other degasser port to an IDEX P-732 manual shut-off valve using a 5cm piece of IDEX 1514L and an XP202 fitting/ferrule.
Connect the shut-off valve to an IDEX P-512 Y-connector using 5cm of IDEX 1514L tubing.
Connect the other arm of the Y-connector to a second shut-off valve using 7cm of tubing.
Connect the free shut-off valve to an IDEX P-678 (or P-696) female luer adapter using 7cm of tubing and an XP-202 fitting/ferrule.

steps.title: Connect Running Buffer Bottle
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 liter glass bottle with an IDEX A-630 cap, closing two holes with an IDEX A-627 filtered plug and an IDEX A-628 plug.

substeps.instruction: Taper one end of a 45cm piece of 1/16" OD tubing and pass it through the open hole of the cap so the tapered end touches the bottle bottom.
Connect the other end to the left port of the syringe pump using an XP-202 fitting and ferrule (Alternatively, route through a free degasser port first).

steps.title: Setup Large Buffer Container
steps.instruction: Prepare a Nalgene style 2019 250ml bottle for the cold incubator.

substeps.instruction: Drill a 1cm diameter hole in the cap and mount an IDEX P-441 bulkhead union.
Place the bottle in the cold incubator.
Connect the left valve to the bulkhead union using 1/16" OD tubing and an XP-202 fitting/ferrule.
Inside the bottle, connect a piece of tubing to the bulkhead union using an XP-202 fitting/ferrule, ensuring the end is tapered and reaches the bottom.

steps.title: Setup Small Buffer Container
steps.instruction: Prepare a Supelco 27162 15ml glass vial with a Supelco 27020 septum cap.

substeps.instruction: Pierce a hole through the rubber septum and run a tube from the valve to the bottom of the vial with a taper-cut end.
Optionally install an IDEX P-603 union in the tube for easier replacement.
Insert a small needle through the septum to prevent vacuum during liquid removal.

steps.title: Install Optional Bubble Trap
steps.instruction: Optionally add an Elvenflow bubble trap between the valve and the degasser using two 5cm pieces of tubing and the provided blue fittings.

steps.title: Assemble 1.5ml Tube Connector
steps.instruction: Construct the cooling and tubing manifold for 10 Eppendorf tubes.

substeps.instruction: 3D print the metal plate adapter (Metal_sheet_cooling_block_adapter.STL) and two tubing holders (Hyb_mix_manifold_1-8-tubbing_1,5Tubes_cold-block_1-5.STL and Hyb_mix_manifold_1-8-tubbing_1,5Tubes_cold-block_6-10.STL).
Push the metal plate adapter into the middle row of a VWR 460-0340 3x5 1.5ml tube block.
Glue a 7x10cm ferrous metal plate (1mm thick) into the slit of the adapter.
Glue two 2mm thick strong magnets to the back of the tubing holders using Loctite.
Latch the tubing holders to the metal plate.
Fix the metal block in the Techne BlocIce using thermal conductive double sided tape (e.g., Elfa Distrelec TCT35).

steps.title: Install Eppendorf Tube Tubing
steps.instruction: Connect the right valve to the 1.5ml tubes.

substeps.instruction: Place the hybmix holder in the cold incubator (optionally secure with thermal conductive glue/sticker).
Cut 10 pieces of 1/8" OD tubing to the length required to reach from the right valve to the bottom of the tubes, with diagonally cut ends.
Mount tubes in the valve and run them through the tubing holder, matching valve numbers to the printed adapter numbers.

steps.title: Finalize Cold Incubator and Waste
steps.instruction: Complete the thermal and waste management setup.

substeps.instruction: Add Labarmour Beads to the cold incubator to ensure buffer contact with the cold plate.
Prepare a 1 liter waste bottle with an IDEX A-630 cap and an IDEX A-627 filtered plug in the big hole.
Run 1/16" OD tubing from the left valve to the waste bottle (entering a few cm).
Position the waste bottle so the hybridization chamber is the lowest point in the system. Use Thorlabs PFS02 cable saddles to fix long lines.

steps.title: Connect Flow Cell
steps.instruction: Connect the Y-connector to the flow cell using 1/16" OD tubing of sufficient length to allow full stage movement.

steps.title: Secure Valve Connections
steps.instruction: Ensure all tubing is properly seated and sealed to prevent leaks.

substeps.instruction: Ensure all tubes are cut flat (using IDEX A-327) and pushed all the way to the back of the valve ports.
For 1/16" OD tubing, apply force until the tube passes the green O-ring, holding the tube 5-10mm from the valve to avoid folding.
Close the valve ring slightly and press tubes again to ensure full insertion.
Tighten the valve ring completely with significant force.

steps.title: Power and Data Connection
steps.instruction: Connect power cables of all machines to an Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) and connect all device USB cables to the computer.

description: Please download this schematic overview of the system: Schematic_ROBOFISH.pdf All parts of the fluidic system are included and labeled with part numbers. The system can dispense arbitrary small volumes to the flow cell that contains the sample. In the top left corner the working of the system is visually explained. The system consists of a syringe pump that is connected to a multi-valve through a 2.5ml reservoir made out of a big tube. The volume of the reservoir matches the volume of the syringe pump. The buffers and the flow cell are all connected to the multi-valve. To dispense a target buffer, the multi-valve connects the buffer to the pump and reservoir. Then the syringe pump aspirates the desired volume (red arrow and red volume). The target buffer volume now sits in the front end of the reservoir. Between the multi-valve and the tissue in the flow cell, there is a dead volume that needs to be bridged. This is caused by the volume in the connecting tubes, the bubble trap and the degasser. To bridge this volume the syringe pump aspirates the same volume of Running-buffer buffer (SSC 2X in the case of smFISH), that is directly connected to the syringe pump, directly into the syringe (blue arrow and dark blue volume). To dispense the target buffer to the flow cell the multi-valve now connects the syringe pump with the flow cell. Then the full contents of the syringe pump, made of the volume of the target buffer and the dead volume, are dispensed so that the target travels over the dead volume and into the flow cell. The system can dispense arbitrary volumes by aspirating them into the reservoir and then use its own Running buffer supply to bridge the dead volume. In systems where buffers are pulled towards the flow cell this is not possible because small volumes will inevitably cause air to be sucked up through the tubes. In this pushing system, aspirated air can simply be expelled by pushing it to the waste port. The system can work with two different flow cells
